--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.find_cohesive_blocks()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find hierarchical cohesive block structure. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.find_cohesive_blocks()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find hierarchical cohesive block structure. title: >- [Graph.find_cohesive_blocks()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Find hierarchical cohesive block structure. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find hierarchical cohesive block structure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L81725-L81828){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.find_cohesive_blocks() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Cohesive blocks](../assets/graphs/find-cohesive-blocks.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The eight-node graph drawn with three nested regions. The whole graph is block 0 with cohesion 1, since removing G cuts off H; A to G is block 1 with cohesion 2 (teal); and the cluster A, B, C, D is block 2 with cohesion 3 (accent). The table lists each block's cohesion, parent block and nodes." width="100%"} Identifies k-cohesive blocks in the graph, where a k-cohesive block is a maximal subgraph that requires removal of at least `k` nodes to disconnect it. Returns a hierarchical structure where child blocks have higher cohesion than their parents (Moody and White, 2003). Each block is split along its minimum node cuts, and the pieces that are more cohesive than the block become its children. A block is left out if it lies inside another block that is at least as cohesive. Edge directions are ignored, as are self-loops and parallel edges. The blocks agree with the k-components of `k_components()`, nested into a hierarchy. Time complexity: exponential in the worst case, since every minimum node cut of every block is enumerated; graphs of a few hundred nodes take seconds. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[int]], list[int], list[int | None]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A tuple containing: (1) blocks, a list of node sets (each as list of node IDs), (2) cohesion, a list of k-values (cohesion of each block), and (3) parent, a list of parent block indices (`None` for root blocks). ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~k_components`) : The same groups, by connectivity level. [](`~node_connectivity`) : The cohesion of a single graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A dense cluster `A, B, C, D` sits inside a ring through `E, F, G`, with `H` hanging off `G`. The whole graph is the root block, with cohesion 1. Leaving out `H` gives a block that needs two nodes removed to split it, and the cluster needs three: ::: {#8240c5ee .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("C", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G"), ("D", "G"), ("G", "H"), ] ) blocks, cohesions, parents = graph.find_cohesive_blocks() label = graph.get_label_from_id ["".join(label(n) for n in b) for b in blocks], cohesions, parents ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['ABCDEFGH', 'ABCDEFG', 'ABCD'], [1, 2, 3], [None, 0, 1]) ``` ::: ::: Each block's parent is the block it lies inside: the cluster's parent is block 1, whose parent is the root, block 0. A complete graph is a single block, as cohesive as a graph on its nodes can be: ::: {#d45323c7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_full_graph(5).find_cohesive_blocks() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]], [4], [None]) ``` ::: ::: ### The core of the metro `metro()` is a made-up city's metro network. Its blocks are the whole network, which a single closure can split, and inside it the 15 stations of the core, which take two: ::: {#05e86590 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} metro = ec.metro() blocks, cohesions, parents = metro.find_cohesive_blocks() [len(b) for b in blocks], cohesions, parents ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ([20, 15], [1, 2], [None, 0]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#aa87b1e1 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} metro.plot(layout="pos", highlight=blocks[1], label_by="label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### How deeply members are embedded Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33). Its blocks nest four levels deep. Giving each member the cohesion of the most cohesive block they belong to shows a core of ten members, both leaders among them, that no three departures could split: ::: {#313755d0 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() blocks, cohesions, parents = karate.find_cohesive_blocks() depth = {} for block, cohesion in zip(blocks, cohesions): for member in block: depth[member] = max(depth.get(member, 0), cohesion) karate.set_node_attrs("cohesion", depth) karate.layout_kamada_kawai().plot( layout="pos", color_by="cohesion", color_scale="sequential", label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Connectivity and flows](../user-guide/connectivity.qmd#measuring-connectivity) finds the structurally cohesive core of the Florentine marriage network with `k_components()`.
